transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Omar (Product), Jordan (VitalCore CTO), Maya (Head of ML), Ethan (Infra), Sara (Compliance)

[00:00] Alex: hey everybody thanks for joining, um quick intro i'm alex with redwood inference, i'm the account lead here, joined by priya our solutions engineer and omar from product, how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Jordan: good thanks alex, excited to see the catalog, we've been poking at open models for a couple months.
[00:12] Maya: yeah hi all, i'm maya, head of ml at vitalcore, main goal today is to understand which open models make sense for our triage/chat workflows and what the latency/costs look like.
[00:20] Priya: awesome, we'll demo the console and the api calls, then show optimize suggestions for batching and quantization; we'll also point out the compatibility matrix for private deployments.
[00:28] Ethan: quick note — our infra team is planning a hybrid: hosted for dev, dedicated reserved for production, with VPC peering into our AWS account. need to confirm KMS and egress.
[00:35] Sara: also need SOC2 controls and audit log detail before we commit.

[03:10] Priya: (screen share) okay here's the model catalog, top section filters by task, cost, and perf profile — selecting 'chat' and 'low-latency' shows Llama2-13B, Mistral-Instruct, and a couple quantized ggml builds. note we show a 'verified perf' badge when we have in-house benchmarks.
[03:35] Jordan: that badge is useful, how often do those benchmarks update?
[03:40] Priya: monthly for major model versions; we also publish per-hardware profiles — e.g., A10 vs A100 vs 80GB A100, and inference runtimes for common seq lengths. small chance of mislabels sometimes in the auto trans, but we try to keep it tight.

[06:02] Alex: quick qualification — can you confirm your target p95 latency for the chat experience and what throughput you expect?
[06:10] Maya: p95 under 600 ms ideally for short prompts (~250 tokens), peak concurrency 150 qps during business hours, but average 20-30 qps.
[06:18] Alex: got it, that's helpful. for that workload we typically recommend a medium-sized open decoder (13B) with 8-bit quant and dedicated pools; Optimize will recommend batching sizes to keep p95 under 600 while reducing per-token cost.

[09:45] Priya: now the compatibility matrix — shows which model variants are supported on Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem). e.g., some aggressive 4-bit quant variants are only available in Dedicated when using our tuned kernels, while ggml-style cpu builds are private-only.
[10:05] Ethan: for private, what's the matrix dependency on CUDA/nv driver versions? we have mixed hosts across k8s clusters.
[10:12] Priya: good question — the matrix lists driver minimums; for our tuned kernels on A100 you need nv 520+, cuTens 22.x ballpark, and for LLM runtime we support both k8s operator and a standalone helm chart. i'll follow up with the exact semver in the compatibility doc.

[12:40] Jordan: benchmarks — are they apples-to-apples? we need to replicate with our tokenization and prompt templates.
[12:48] Priya: yes the public benchmarks use our canonical prompts and tokenization; for accuracy we show perplexity/ROUGE for eval sets, and latency/cost per-token for infra shapes. we can run a tailored benchmark — bring your prompts and we'll run it in a sandbox or run it in your VPC via a short POC.
[13:23] Maya: what's the expected delta when switching from fp16 to 8-bit quant? we saw big drops in accuracy for some of our generative outputs on previous vendors.
[13:31] Priya: it varies by model; some models are robust to 8-bit quant, others need 4-bit with calibration to match quality. in Optimize we show quality regression estimates from our eval harness; e.g., for Mistral-Instruct 8-bit shows a 1.2% drop on our summarization set, but latency improves 2.5x. we recommend a canary rollout with evaluation prompts.

[16:00] Alex: competition question — are you evaluating other vendors?
[16:05] Jordan: yes some teams are testing Anthropic and OpenAI for the higher-quality path; procurement also asked about Vertex AI for unified infra.
[16:12] Alex: makes sense — we typically emphasize cost predictability and the unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private as a differentiator.

[18:30] Priya: demoing the API: simple REST call for chat generation, streaming supported; function/tool-calling also works for structured extraction. here's a sample curl with model-id redwood/mistral-instruct-13b-8q. note the model-id in the catalog includes quantization and hardware compatibility suffix.
[19:05] Maya: will we be able to pin model versions for rollouts? we need pins for regulatory traceability.
[19:10] Priya: yes, the console supports pinning and versioned rollouts — canary, A/B, auto-fallback to a lower-cost variant if latency spikes. audit logs capture model-version changes for compliance.

[22:17] Ethan: what about network egress — hosted calls vs private? we need data residency and some payloads cannot leave the VPC.
[22:25] Omar: for Private deployments you can keep inference inside the VPC/on-prem; for Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private endpoints to avoid public egress. we'll provide the network whitepaper.
[22:40] Sara: also KMS integration — our infosec insists on CMKs and HSM-backed keys for PHI.
[22:48] Priya: we integrate with AWS KMS and external HSMs; we log key usage and can support envelope encryption. i'll add the KMS integration guide in the follow-up.

[26:00] Priya: showing the Optimize tab — it recommends batching, prefix caching, and which models to try based on token distribution. e.g., for short prompts prefix caching can cut repeat context perf by up to 30%. for your workload with many similar triage prompts, caching helps a lot.
[26:30] Maya: can Optimize propose quantization profiles?
[26:35] Priya: yes, it suggests 8-bit or 4-bit presets with predicted quality deltas and cost savings. you can simulate cost on 'sample workload' and it will estimate monthly savings.

[29:50] Jordan: what's the onboarding timeline if we pick Dedicated? procurement cycles are long, around 8-10 weeks.
[29:58] Alex: typical path: pilot in hosted (2-4 weeks) -> POC on Dedicated (4-6 weeks) -> contract for Reserved capacity (4-8 weeks) depending on legal. we can compress some stages if procurement is ready.

[33:10] Maya: for the POC, we want a benchmark comparing Llama2-13B-8q vs Mistral-7B-8q vs a 13B ggml variant in our infra. can you run that?
[33:18] Priya: yes we can — we'll propose a POC runbook and a benchmark spreadsheet template. suggest 3 prompts and a couple of eval metrics (latency p95, per-token cost, and quality score).

[35:40] Ethan: side question — what monitoring and tracing do you provide? we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards.
[35:48] Omar: Console has per-model/per-route dashboards, traces (sampled), and token-cost attribution. you can stream logs to your SIEM too.

[37:55] Sara: compliance — please send SOC2 report and that audit log retention policy. also, do you support SAML for SSO?
[38:03] Alex: yes SAML/SSO, RBAC and audit logs. we'll attach SOC2 cert and the retention options.

[40:20] Alex: recap — we'll send: model catalog PDF + compatibility matrix link, tailored benchmark spreadsheet, SOC2/KMS docs, and a POC runbook. Priya will own the POC runbook, i'll send pricing and contract timelines.
[40:35] Jordan: great, thanks. let's target next Tue for the POC scoping call.
[40:42] Maya: i'll share sample prompts and datasets by Friday.
[40:48] Priya: perfect, we'll get the bench scheduled once we have the prompts.
[41:05] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with calendar invites and links.
[41:10] (call ended)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts in product names (e.g., 'K-V cash' for KV cache) and minor speaker overlaps. References shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/model-catalog (deck), https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/vitalcore-bench.xlsx (bench template), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf (security pack).
